one_month_reasoning: One scheduled event falls in the window: Q3 2026 earnings on 2026-10-29, before the open. Consensus is about $9.8 EPS on $22.2-22.4B revenue, below Q2's $23.0B, so the revenue bar looks low. Trefis counts 19 LLY earnings days over five years: 53% up, with a median gain of +4.5% and a median loss of -3.5%. That is close to symmetric, with a slight positive skew. FY2027 revisions are running 19 up to 4 down, and Lilly beat by $1.98 in Q2. Against that, Foundayo scripts trail the Wegovy pill (about 34k vs 172k a week in August), US realized price fell 9% last quarter, and Medicaid MFN was extended in September, so the call could revive the pricing worry. The full TRIUMPH-2 retatrutide data came out at EASD on 2026-09-30 and the stock fell 2.3% that day, so that catalyst is already behind us. Over five years the base rate says there is little edge in earnings direction. I add only a small positive drift: median about $1,155, +0.5%. For spread I use a mix of 80% lognormal at sigma 9% and 20% at sigma 15%. That averages to roughly the 10% monthly vol implied by 35% annual vol / 3.5, with fatter tails for a possible ±10% earnings gap. The ladder is essentially unchanged from my capped run.

fair_value.method: A three-way blend. (1) 22.5x NTM EPS as of Oct 2027 of about $53.3 (0.25 x 2027 consensus of $47.3 + 0.75 x 2028E of $55.3), about $1,199, weight 50%. (2) 27x TTM EPS as of Oct 2027 of about $44.5, about $1,201, weight 30%. (3) A base-rate drift of today's $1,149.85 x 1.04, about $1,196, weight 20%. The blend is about $1,199, rounded to $1,200.

bear.story: Price erosion outruns volume. MFN goes beyond Medicaid and the government channel, the Bridge lapses after 2027, Foundayo stays a distant second to the Wegovy pill, and HSBC's $80-120B peak-market view starts to look right. 2027 EPS is cut toward $42 and the multiple falls to about 19x, in a partial replay of Gilead's 2016 HCV de-rating (-29% in a year) or Novo's 2024-26 collapse (-74%). A recession, at 24-35% odds by end-2027, would hit the roughly 80% of scripts that are cash-pay.

base.story: Volume keeps outrunning price. 2027 EPS lands near $47, the retatrutide BLA is filed in Q1 2027 with approval likely late 2027 (Kalshi about 45-49% by mid-2027 and about 90% by end-2027), and the stock trades at about 22-23x NTM EPS of about $53, a little under the $1,329 average Street target.

bull.story: Revision momentum continues (2027 consensus has risen from $41.9 in April to $47.3), Foundayo inflects with reimbursement and the LMIC push, and retatrutide is approved early on priority review. 2028 EPS goes above $58, the multiple holds at about 26-27x, and the price approaches Citi's $1,600 Street-high target.

thesis_break_reason: $850 is about 26% below today and equals 18x 2027 consensus EPS of $47.3. That is below anything LLY has traded at on forward earnings in the GLP-1 era, and it is near HSBC's bear target. A trade there would most likely mean estimates are breaking: a GLP-1 net-price collapse, MFN extended to commercial pricing, a retatrutide safety or regulatory setback, or the Bridge or coverage unwinding. Ordinary volatility would not do it. LLY's worst drawdowns in recent years were about 33-34% (Aug 2025) and 23% (2026), so a 26% fall alone is not decisive. Below $850 with consensus EPS falling would be.

reasoning: Base rates first. LLY's realized vol is 35%. Its earnings-day reactions are near-symmetric: 53% up, medians +4.5% and -3.5%. Its annual max drawdowns have run 15-34%. The #1 company in a sector has historically lagged it by 3-4% a year over 1-10 years (Arnott 'top dog'). The two best analogs for a dominant franchise facing a price war are Gilead in 2016 (HCV sales -22%, stock -29%) and Novo in 2024-26 (-74%, forward P/E about 12x); both justify a fat left tail. LLY's fundamentals point the other way: Q2 revenue +48%, FY26 guidance raised to $85-87B, and 2027 consensus up from $41.9 in April to $47.3 now (19 up / 4 down in 30 days). Retatrutide's Phase 3 package is complete, a BLA is due in Q1 2027, and Kalshi gives about 90% for approval by end-2027. Tariff risk is small because LLY's MFN agreement exempts it from the Section 232 pharma tariff. The newly found negatives are Foundayo's slow ramp (about 34k vs 172k weekly scripts for the Wegovy pill), the Medicaid MFN extension in Sept 2026, the Bridge expiring in Dec 2027, and a 2.3% drop on the full TRIUMPH-2 data on 9/30, which suggests good news is priced in. My fair value comes down from $1,240 to $1,200 (22.5x NTM EPS of about $53.3, blended with 27x TTM and a +4% base-rate drift), which is about +4% expected drift. The distribution is a three-lognormal mixture: bear $810 (22%, sigma 0.28), base $1,200 (55%, sigma 0.20), bull $1,560 (23%, sigma 0.20). Its median is about $1,200 and P(>= spot) is about 0.56. No option data was consulted, and nothing under priors/ was opened.
